To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the material we isolated from spleen tissue, which increases vascular permeabillity, is a complex mixture of proteins of molecular weight 50,000 to 100,000 and that this activity can be increased or decreased by chemical modification of specific functional groups of the protein molecule.
SPF is a complex mixture of proteins which increases vascular permeabilty by a mechanism which involves the release of histamines and 5-HT.
the permeability factor from spleen tissue is a complex mixture of proteins which are modified by carboxylate groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of a protein which increases vascular permeabilty and causes a local inflammatory reaction in the skin of the host.
the isolation and characterization of the high molecular weight protein fraction of SPF which causes the increase in vascular permeabilty in the first 20 minutes after intradermal administration.
the isolation from spleen of a protein extract which increases vascular permeabilty in vivo, and with the investigation of its chemical and pharmacological characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPF is a protein extract of spleen which causes a marked increase of vascular permeability in a variety of species.
SPF is a complex mixture of proteins, the active component(s) of which is/are probably not the result of a single structural motif but of the presence of a number of different chemical features.
SPF appears to be an endogenous protein, the activity of which depends on the presence of carboxylate groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the permeability factor from spleen tissue is a mixture of proteins with molecular weights between 50, 000 and 100000.
SPF is a mixture of proteins which cause the release of histamin and 5-HT from mast cells and platelets.
SPF is a mixture of proteins of molecular weight 50,000–100,000 which are active in the presence of amines and which are not esterases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vascular permeability factor is a complex mixture of proteins which are not necessarily related to one another.
a number of proteins can cause vascular permeability.
SPF is a mixture of proteins which cause an increase in vascular permeabillity by releasing mediators from the cells of the inflammatory reaction.
